newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland sugar to break five MT barrier - QSC.
newsitem.headline: Queensland sugar to break five MT barrier - QSC.

text.p: The key Australian sugar producing state of Queensland expected another year of record sugar production in 1997, estimates released by Queensland Sugar Corp (QSC) on Thursday showed.

QSC's chief executive David Rutledge said Queensland's 1997 season raw sugar production would reach five million tonnes actual for the first time and was expected to exceed 1996 season production of 4.99 million tonnes by about three percent, he said.
This would bring production to about 5.14 million tonnes.

Rutledge's projections indicate total Australian raw sugar production in 1997 of about 5.43 million tonnes, if the minor sugar state of New South Wales produces the at the same level as last year's 285,000 tonnes from a cane crush of 2.38 million tonnes.
Australia's total sugar production in 1996 was 5.26 million tonnes actual.
Queensland's 1997 season cane crop had suffered the effects of cyclone Justin in March, although the extent of damage would not be known for a few weeks, Rutledge said.

"Initial reports indicate that the sugar content of cane affected by the cyclone will be lower this year but a clear picture will emerge as crushing commences in all areas over the next few weeks," Rutledge said.
World sugar prices could improve over the next 12 months as the 1996/97 Thai and Indian crops were lower than expected and sugar consumption in Russia was expected to increase, he said.
Demand for Queensland's raw sugar had remained strong in both domestic and international markets, he said.

"Although we are selling into an oversupplied market place, the demand for our product from both traditional and new customers is more than keeping pace with our own increases in production," Rutledge said.
QSC had already successfully marketed most of the current season's raw sugar production.
It would be unable to supply several markets it had sold to in 1996/97 despite record production, he said.
The Queensland cane crush season began in Proserpine last week with the rest of Queensland's 25 sugar mills expected to start crushing by mid-July.
